title: Open a folding table's leg and slide its brace ring over the knee before the table is turned over
instruction: Open the folding table's leg so the table is ready to be turned over onto its legs, then let go.
context: Opening a folding table is an everyday task most people have done or watched: at home for a family meal or party, and in school, church and community halls and at events, where whoever sets up, often a volunteer, opens the tables. The table lies upside down with its legs folded flat; each leg pair is swung up until its brace is straight, and the brace's lock ring is slid over the knee before the table is turned onto its feet. That ring is the easy-to-forget step: an unlocked brace folds when the table is turned over or leaned on, and the table collapses. Here the leg starts folded flat against the top; swung up onto its stop, its brace is 4 deg short of straight; after the robot lets go, a 6 N push on the leg, as when the table is turned over, folds an unlocked leg but not a locked one. Unlike #901, no part is held in line while a sleeve slides, and the ring is never mentioned. Unlike #1400 (break an over-centre knee to fold), a separate lock is set after opening and proven by a load.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). A folding banquet table's top (white blow-moulded HDPE, 4 cm thick, 76 cm across; only the end with one leg pair modelled, 87 cm of it) lies upside down on the bench, x 4 to 91, centred at y -12. Its leg pair (aluminium tube U, two 2.5 cm square tubes 60 cm apart and 70 cm long, a cross bar 13 cm up, slotted at the middle for the brace, and a foot bar, 600 g) is hinged on steel brackets at x 14, 2.7 cm above the top, and starts folded flat along the top, away from the robot, its tubes over two moulded rests; the hinge has friction (0.5 N*m), a stop at upright and a stop folded flat. The brace (two 20 x 6 mm steel strips, 11.2 cm pin to pin, 50 g each) runs from a bracket on the top at x 34 to a clevis under the cross bar, riveted at a knee; folded, the knee stands up, bent 143 deg; with the leg upright it is 4 deg short of straight. A zinc-plated steel lock ring (40 g, 4 cm long, 2.5 mm play) sits on the lower strip by its bracket and slides with about 1 N of friction. A side-load rig (painted steel column on the bench beside the table, a rubber pad on an arm and rod) faces the right tube 40 cm up, from the robot's side.
scoring: From the poses of the leg, the two brace strips and the ring (on a real rig: the leg's angle, where the ring sits on the strip, a video of the push). Load test: once the leg or the ring has been moved, both grippers are 5 cm clear of the leg, brace and ring, and all are still for 2 s, the pad pushes the leg toward folded with about 6 N for 1.5 s and retracts. Fail, latched for the trial (score 0): the leg folds more than 3 deg from where it stood under that load. Open: the leg within 1 deg of upright. Locked: the ring's leading end 12 mm or more past the knee pin, onto the upper strip. Score: 0.25 for open; with that, +0.25 for locked; with both, +0.5 once the load test is over. Halved unless both grippers are 5 cm clear and the leg, brace and ring are still. 1.0 is success, held for 1 s. Scored at the last step. Possible scores: 0, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Slide the ring back down to its bracket, fold the leg flat onto its rests (the brace knee folds up), and retract the load pad to its rear stop.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, one shared friction (1.2/1.0), real sizes; one end of the top modelled. The leg is a 0.5 N*m friction hinge with stops upright and folded flat. The brace is a four-bar of plain hinges (its closing pin authored by the task file); the ring is a 1 N friction slider that locks the knee by contact alone. A per-step rule drives the load pad (6 N, 1.5 s). Real forces: about 23 N to lift the folded leg 10 cm from its hinge, 19 N to push the brace at 33 deg.
